title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in an Austin neighborhood while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a perception or response failure in a deployed system, where the vehicle either did not detect the animal or did not treat it as an obstacle requiring avoidance.

The failure occurred during live operation on public streets rather than in testing conditions. A human safety operator was in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the incident. It is not established whether the operator could have reasonably detected and prevented the collision in the time available, or what the vehicle's training data or decision rules specified about small animals in traffic.

Avride investigated a separate allegation that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no evidence to support it. The company has since excluded certain streets from testing and stated it is evaluating technology improvements. Whether these changes will address animal detection or response is not specified.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The duck was well-known to residents because it nested outside a local Italian restaurant. Local residents discovered duck eggs at the scene and have placed them in an incubator for safekeeping.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and investigated claims that it failed to stop at a stop sign, concluding no evidence supported this allegation. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now evaluating technology improvements to prevent similar situations. Avride continues autonomous vehicle testing in other areas, and multiple companies including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate self-driving vehicles throughout Austin.
